comments.note: DapperMovieRepository.GetOriginalFilenameAsync uses LIMIT 1 without an ORDER BY — movies_filenames has no insertion-timestamp column (confirmed by schema), so no deterministic ordering is possible. A comment explaining this is the only option until an audit-timestamp column is added in a future schema revision.

SharedConnectionFactory / NonDisposingConnection is duplicated verbatim in DapperMovieCatalogRepositoryTests, DapperFilterSlotRepositoryTests, LibraryScannerIntegrationTests, and the new DapperMovieRepositoryTests. A shared test-infrastructure helper class in the Infrastructure.Tests project would eliminate this duplication.

The private MovieRow class inside DapperMovieRepository requires a comment explaining why a plain class with public setters is used instead of a record (Dapper reflection cannot access positional record constructors when the type is private). The comment was added inline but a constraints.md entry was also added for future reference.

DapperMovieRepository.SaveAsync does not update review/review_message or watch_count — these are intentionally split into SetReviewAsync and ResetViewCountAsync. This is by design per the IMovieRepository contract but is not obvious from the method signature alone; a comment on SaveAsync clarifying the intentional scope would prevent future accidental inclusion.

summary: Reviewed 5 files (Movie.cs, IMovieRepository.cs, DapperMovieRepository.cs, IAppPaths.cs, AppPaths.cs). 0 Critical, 0 High, 0 Medium, 2 Low, 1 Info. Security sign-off: PASS. All SQL queries use Dapper parameterized syntax exclusively — no string concatenation; SQL injection risk is fully mitigated. The Movie record is immutable (required/init properties). No secrets, no auth surfaces, no deserialization of untrusted data in the modified code.

comments.note: A03 — SQL Injection (Info/Positive): All 7 DapperMovieRepository methods (GetByIdAsync, SaveAsync, ResetViewCountAsync, SetReviewAsync, GetOriginalFilenameAsync, GetKnownActorNamesAsync, GetKnownStudiosAsync) use parameterized Dapper queries with @Param syntax. No string concatenation into SQL. No injection vectors detected.

A04 — Insecure Design (Low): DapperMovieRepository.SaveAsync intentionally omits review/review_message and watch_count to restrict scope to editable fields only. This separation of concerns (SaveAsync vs SetReviewAsync/ResetViewCountAsync) is a sound security design choice — it prevents accidental overwrite of review state during a save operation.

A09 — Security Logging (Low/Info): SetReviewAsync modifies the needsReview flag and review_message, which are editorially sensitive fields. No audit log entry is written for these changes. For the current desktop / local-DB use case the risk is low, but if multi-user or networked access is added in the future, audit logging for review-flag mutations should be considered.
